Everything that happens between people and companies in KORbuild reaches you in two places: the bell inside the app and, for some notices, an email. The notices are recorded by the database itself when the event happens, so they are the same on every device and never depend on one phone being open.

The bell is at the top of every screen. A red number counts what you have not read. Tap a notice to open the screen it is about; it becomes read, on every device. The bell with the latest notices: the newest first, unread ones highlighted The bell also shows the reminders the phone works out by itself (the 4 pm daily report reminder, a late daily report, a late schedule stage, a punch with no clock-out). Those exist only on the device and are never emailed.

This guide is for the person who will present KORbuild to a customer. You do not need to know the system beforehand: follow the order below, sign in with the users indicated, and use the "what to say" boxes as your script. The full presentation — Daily, Crew, Measure and Settings — takes about 40 minutes; with questions, plan for an hour. For a shorter meeting, pick the acts that matter to the customer.

Construction companies in the US run their jobs on paper, text messages and spreadsheets. The superintendent writes the daily report at night (or not at all), the office chases people by phone, and when a client disputes a delay there is no reliable record of what happened on site. KORbuild is one platform, one set of jobs and people, with modules the company turns on as it needs them: Module In one sentence Who uses it Daily The daily construction report, filled out on the phone in minutes, approved by the office and shared with the client as a sealed PDF. Daily is the daily construction report (in Portuguese, RDO). Every workday, the subcontractor's person in charge on site records the weather, the crew, the equipment, the work performed, the issues and the photos. The general contractor of the job reviews and approves the report — or the subcontractor itself, on a job it has directly with the owner — and the approved report is sealed and shared with the client as a link or a PDF. See How KORbuild is organized.

A record that holds up. When a client disputes a delay, the daily reports are the contractor's evidence: rain that stopped the pour, a late delivery, a missing inspection. Photos carry date, time and GPS inside the image, and the approved report is sealed. Reports that actually get done. Each job has a person responsible for its report, a daily deadline (6 PM) and reminders. The office sees the next morning which jobs did not report. Minutes, not an evening. On the phone, the foreman copies yesterday's report, adjusts the crew, dictates what was done and takes the photos. It works without sign

This manual walks through Daily one task at a time. The first part is for the field (on the phone); the second, for the office (on the computer). Screen names, buttons and messages are written exactly as they appear in KORbuild, in bold. Before you start Daily opens in the area of your role: the field starts on Today, the office on the Dashboard. On the phone, the menu is at the bottom of the screen; on the computer, on the left. If you do not see a screen described here, your role does not include it — see Roles and permissions.

texto: What it is for: knowing, at a glance, which reports you owe and which ones the office sent back. Who can do it Anyone who fills out daily reports (default role: Foreman). Tap the job to fill it out now. yellow — today's report is missing: jobs without today's report, with the deadline and the time left (for example, Due: today at 6 PM · 1h30 left). red — the office requested changes: a report sent back, with the reason i

titulo: Field: fill out the daily report
texto: What it is for: recording the day on the job: weather, crew, equipment, what was done, what got in the way, and photos. Who can do it The person responsible for the job's report, or anyone with Fill out daily reports (default role: Foreman). On Today, tap the job. The job screen shows the date, the deadline and the previous reports. Tap New daily report to start blank, or or copy from a previous report to start from another day (see Copy a previous report). The weather is pulled automatically from the job location for the morning (7 AM–12 PM) and the afternoon (1 PM–5 PM). With more than 2 mm of rain in a period, that period is marked Not workable. Check or correct each period: Sunny, Cloudy or Rain, and Workable or Not workable. Get weather automatically fetches it again (it needs signal). The report says whether the weather was automatic, adjusted by hand or entered by hand. Weather, morning and afternoon

Tap the trades (+ Mason, + Laborer, + Carpenter…) to add them, then use − and + to set how many were Present and Absent. A trade that is not in the list: type it in Other trade and tap Add. Update from the crew that clocked in fills the crew from the people who clocked in on this job today in Crew (the time clock). The section shows the total present (for example, 13 present). Crew: present and absent by trade
Add the equipment on site with its quantity and status: Running, Idle or Under maintenance. Equipment on site

Each activity has: Field What to enter Description What was done. Example: poured the 2nd floor slab, 60 cu yd. Location / phase Where on the job (floor, building, area). Status In progress or Completed. Schedule task and % complete Only when the job has a schedule: the task this activity advanced and how far it is now. The schedule is updated when the office approves the report. Dictate: speak instead of typing (uses the phone's voice recognition). Anything that got in the way of the day: tap the type (Material / delivery, Rain, Equipment, Safety / accident, Crew / absences, Visit / inspection, Design / conflict, Other) and describe what happened and the impact. Why it matters This is the section that protects the contractor in a delay claim: rain that stopped the pour, a late delivery, an inspection that did not show up — recorded on the day it happened. Take photo opens the camera; From gallery picks existing photos. Each photo gets a stamp inside the image with the job, date, time and GPS coordinates, and is reduced on the phone (for example, 4.2 MB becomes about 300 KB) so it uploads fast even on a weak signal. Add a caption to each photo (for example, rebar before the pour). If the phone has no GPS, the job's location is used, and the stamp says so. Photos: camera or gallery

The bar at the bottom says what is still missing — for example, Missing: at least one person in manpower, at least one activity described — or that the report is ready. Then tap Submit for approval. You can leave the report and come back later.

What it is for: most days look like the day before. Copying saves typing. On the job screen, tap or copy from a previous report. Choose the report to copy from (the most recent comes selected) and tap Copy. Choose which report to copy The new report brings the crew (with absences reset to zero), the equipment and the activities still in progress. Weather, photos and issues are not copied: they belong to the day.

What it is for: a workday without work on the job (rain, holiday, job on hold) still needs a record — it justifies the day and stops the reminders. On the job screen, tap No work today. Choose the reason: Rain / unworkable weather, Holiday or day off, Job put on hold by the client, Material shortage, Strike or work stoppage or Other reason, and add a note if you want. Tap Log it. The day is recorded as that day's report, it goes to the office and the reminders for that day stop.

If a past workday has no report, it appears in the red late report box on Today (up to the last 3 workdays). Tap it and fill out the report as usual — you can also copy from a previous one. A report submitted after the deadline is accepted, but it is marked Submitted late in the report and in the PDF, with the date and time of the first submission and the deadline it missed.

titulo: Fix a report the office sent back
texto: On Today, the red box The office requested changes to report #… shows the job, the date and the reason, in quotes. Tap Fix now →. The report opens with the request at the top. Make the changes and tap Resubmit. A request for changes on the foreman's Today screen A resubmission after a request for changes does not count as late: what counts is the first submission.

Nothing special to do: KORbuild works offline. While you fill out the report, everything is saved on the phone. If you submit without signal, the report is Saved on this device and waits in a queue. As soon as the connection comes back, it uploads by itself, photo by photo, and the office receives it. After the first visit, the whole app opens without internet. The indicator at the top of the screen (Online) shows the connection. In the prototype Tap Online to simulate losing the signal, and tap again to come back online.
History lists every report you filled out, newest first, with its status (Draft, Awaiting approval, Changes requested, Approved). Tap one to open it. History on the phone

Settings is where each company sets up KORbuild once, for every module: the company profile, the people (employees and users), what each role can do, the jobs and their schedules, the contacts, and — for companies that clock in their crews — the labor burden and the work rules. Nothing that a company may want to change is hard-coded. Settings comes with every plan, at no extra cost. Each company has its own Settings and never sees another company's (see How KORbuild is organized).
